industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, with the sector rows carrying a view that moved inside the industry this week: Software B2B Enterprise goes to Neutral on the rotation into software, Semiconductors stays Underweight on the AI capital spending re-pricing, Hardware stays Neutral with the evidence moved against it at the margin. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): the market has stopped paying for AI capital spending (hyperscaler prints gave no lift, ABB sold on data-centre orders) while demand is intact and sub-sector upgrades continue (memory, equipment, power electronics), and the software-against-semiconductors factor pair is reversing (Goldman Sachs' desk, 26 October). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: B now, B prior. The industry row stays C because the industry is split by the rotation itself. Counter-case for D: the Nasdaq down 6% in two weeks with momentum down 15% is a regime statement about this industry; for B: the only industry with upgrades inside the sell-off.

sector.why: Neutral, from Underweight, because the thematics read turned: the broadening trade has moved into software. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): Nordic software 'is working again', up 9% in a month as AI-disruption fears faded while hardware gives back gains (Danske Bank TMT, 27 October), and Goldman Sachs' desk (26 October) reports the software-against-semiconductors factor pair reversing, so two houses now describe the same rotation; against it the discount-rate case still holds (the US ten-year above 5%, the Fed hiking in December) and one software sector is not another (Fortinet down 20%, ServiceNow down 16%, cybersecurity broken; Outset Global, 29 October). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: A now, C prior, the market now ranks the sector first. Balanced, so Neutral by judgement, not Overweight: a row valued off a yield cannot be Overweight with the ten-year above 5%. Seven Pool names (Sinch and Sectra in the top twelve of the starting score, QT Group, Truecaller, Yubico, Planisware, SAP). Counter-case: the recovery is one month old in one region and the discount rate is rising. To B if the Fed path is marked down with relative strength holding A or B; back to D if relative strength falls to C with the ten-year still above 5%.

geography.why: Neutral, carried. No Swedish survey and no Riksbank reading reached the pack this week, so the condition for B (a confidence print at or above normal with the Riksbank on hold) could not be tested; the only Swedish data point is food retail volumes up 5.3% in September after a value-added tax cut (Danske, 18 Oct), which is a sector fact, not a country view. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43). Four live holdings are Swedish (Avanza 0.50%, Hexatronic 4.95%, Sdiptech 5.05%, Xvivo 5.05%, 15.55 points), judged in component 4 and in amendment 10. Relative strength is not graded by country.

memo.verdict: Neutral; park; conviction medium (the direction is clear, the timing of the clearing is not). The park rule applies because predictability ('Transmission', RA 8, E 2, BB 4) is D and the record does not argue otherwise: the thing the case turns on is a supplier's policy (Autodesk's partner terms) that is disclosed after the fact. Management at C, business quality at C and trackability at C do not park it. The case re-opens on evidence the company can deliver (Design Management EBITA at or above SEK 100m on 23 October 2026 with the savings run-rate confirmed; contract-duration disclosure; positive Design organic growth in Q1 2027) or on a price below SEK 48.5, where the three-year modal return clears the 20 percent bar. The record's one-line bet: that Autodesk has finished changing the terms, so that a SEK 100m cost-out and a 2027 renewal cohort restore Design Management's profit and the market pays the sector's 14 to 15x for it instead of 12x. Primary 'Target Setup': 'Major CfC Clearing', fitted at C, no secondary.
case: The change is external and adverse, and the internal answer is defensive. In 2026 Autodesk cut renewal commissions (about SEK 20m of net sales a quarter, about SEK 80m a year), withdrew the multi-year discounts, and about one-third of three-year contracts are moving permanently to one-year terms; the three-year renewal cohort came up thin in Q2 2026 after Q2 2025 carried SEK 80m of early renewals (SEK 70m of EBITA). Design's EBITA fell from SEK 162m to SEK 33m in Q2 2026. The company's answer: a SEK 100m Symetri cost programme (half in 2026, all by 2027, for a SEK 28m charge; PLM's prior programme delivered SEK 45m and lifted the PLM margin to 9.4 percent in Q2 2026 from 0.9 percent in Q1 2025), a pause in acquisitions to bring leverage back under 2.5x (10 deals in 2025 for SEK 1,819m took it to 2.4x), and a slow tilt to proprietary software (own software and services +7 percent organically in Q2 2026). The only clear tailwinds (Swedish infrastructure from SEK 94bn to SEK 130bn by 2027; defence to SEK 175bn in 2026; NIS2, the Cyber Resilience Act, CSRD, German BIM mandates) act on Process Management (sales +18 percent to SEK 463m in Q2 2026, organic 2 percent on election delays, margin 20.1 percent after eight consecutive quarters of improvement) and on about 15 percent of PLM in aerospace and defence; construction (Europe construction PMI 42.8 in June 2026; US ABI 44.5 in May 2026) and German automotive are contracting. Seat demand is intact (customer base up year on year; Autodesk's own design revenue +18 percent; Mensch und Maschine's Digitization +12 percent); the weakness is in contract length and the supplier's terms.

'Change Forces' is D: the framework's screen rule (three strong internal forces, or a chief-executive change plus a guidance increase) is not met; one force is strong ('Standards improvement' B), two moderate (the capital-markets-day targets C; the strategy tilt C), the balance sheet is spent (KQ 11 D), no chief-executive change (F), no perimeter reduction (F), no shareholder-returns increase (F). 'External forces' D: supply F (the force that broke the quarter), demand D, competition D (the tightening comes from the supplier moving down the chain, not rivals), macro D (a weaker dollar cut H1 2026 sales by SEK 108m and EBITA by SEK 26m, unhedged; 65 percent of sales outside SEK), cycle C (a dated low turning by arithmetic in 2027), disruption C (AI seat-compression fear strengthening in the market, disproved in operations so far), political and regulatory B.

'Financial Outputs' is D: three of four outputs worse in 2026 than in any of the last three years; only cash conversion improving (B), and that is the reversal of a working-capital outflow. 'Sell-side upgrades' D: dashboard revisions F, revision skew F (no broker raised), upgrade record D (FY2023 margin 8.6 percent against a 10 percent floor; the January 2026 Design-growth claim withdrawn in April; the Q1 2026 restatement of 7 May 2026; the Q2 2026 adjusted EBITA miss of 11 percent), commentary C (Redeye calls 17 percent unachievable near-term; the named upgrade scope is Design EBITA of SEK 109m in Q3 2026 per DNB Carnegie and the 2027 renewal turn), modal forecast C (our FY2026 about SEK 3.80 against a consensus median of SEK 4.01 on 2 brokers; FY2027 about SEK 4.15 against a mixed-basis median of SEK 3.94), guidance versus consensus C (the gap is a credibility gap, not a conservatism signal). 'Goldilocks growth' D: negative over six months, about 9 percent a year over eighteen months, about 8 percent over three years. 'Staircase' C: dated, company-delivered and fully understood (the Q3 2026 report; the 2027 comparisons against -6 and -11 percent; the full SEK 100m run-rate; leverage below 2x; the restart of acquisitions), with nothing that extends rather than restores.
counter_case: At Building Block 1, the strongest form: the market has mistaken a reporting artefact for a structural break. Design's customers are still there (customer counts up year on year; Autodesk's own design revenue grew 18 percent); the Q2 2026 collapse was SEK 70m of prior-year pull-forward plus a SEK 28m one-off charge; underlying Q2 2026 EBITA of SEK 176m beat the comparable SEK 168m; the cost-out is SEK 100m against a SEK 80m-a-year headwind; so 2027 EBITA runs above SEK 1bn and EPS above SEK 4.5, and at 12.9x the shares re-rate to 18x on the first clean quarter. The record concedes the base effect, the customer counts and the cost-out, and holds its view because the structural part is not a base effect: one-third of three-year contracts are moving permanently to one-year terms, the renewal commission cut recurs every quarter, Autodesk's direct share keeps rising, the Q1 2026 figures were restated, and management has said it cannot expect organic growth in Design; a clean quarter restores the 2025 level and does not make the growth rate material.

At Building Block 2: the foundations are exceptionally high-quality, the research's own verdict at high confidence: a 90-acquisition record, 18 percent EBITA compound growth over a decade, 63 to 70 percent recurring revenue, negative working capital, a public-sector lock-in no peer has, and the agent model protects the partner (street-price discipline, no credit risk, higher reported margins). The record concedes the record, the public-sector moat and the asset-light economics, and holds because the question is robustness under the expected change, which is in Design, whose gross margin the vendor sets and has cut three times in two years, whose nearest peer executed better, and whose earnings base is the least transparent in the group.
triggers: - Re-open the case: Design EBITA at or above SEK 100m on 23 October 2026 with the savings run-rate confirmed; contract-duration disclosure (which DNB Carnegie names as the re-rating trigger); positive Design organic growth in Q1 2027; or a price below SEK 48.5 (three-year modal return at the bar; eighteen-month SEK 55.5).

- Move the full-clearing odds to probable: Design EBITA above SEK 109m on 23 October 2026 (DNB Carnegie's forecast) and positive Design organic growth in Q1 2027. Move the failure branch to modal: Design EBITA below SEK 80m, or an Autodesk direct-billing announcement for Europe.

- Alarm levels: Design EBITA below SEK 80m in Q3 2026; realised savings below SEK 80m by Q4 2026; net debt to EBITDA above 2.5x at any quarter-end; two quarters of Process Management organic growth below 2 percent or a margin below 19 percent; the US ABI below 45 for three months.

- Invalidate levels: a second consecutive quarter of Design organic decline worse than -5 percent after Q1 2027; net debt to EBITDA above 2.9x including earn-outs; Autodesk direct-sales mix above 69 percent, or direct billing announced for Europe.

- Open questions the record could not settle: the EPS basis gap (brokers' SEK 4.18 against reported SEK 2.87 in FY2025; SEK 1.31 a share not fully explained; whether the add-back includes the SEK 130m of capitalised-development amortisation, which would take the 'Modal return' to D); the one-year to three-year contract mix (not disclosed; the first data gap); the overlap with the framework's own historical errors (the track-record and lessons files not among the inputs); the live thematics file (not among the inputs).

- Series to watch: Design Management EBITA and organic growth (quarterly); own-software and services organic growth (quarterly; 7 percent in Q2 2026); Autodesk's direct-sales mix and partner-programme announcements (quarterly); Mensch und Maschine's Digitization growth (quarterly; the first thing to check); the Europe construction PMI and the German manufacturing PMI (monthly); cash conversion against 70 percent of EBITA (half-yearly; expected by H2 2026); the FY2026 dividend (our path SEK 1.15; consensus SEK 1.23 for FY2027, SEK 1.40 for FY2028); the buy share (100 percent; the next move can only be down).
